A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of VIRES. Their text, equations, Tables 1–5, Figures 1–11, and Section 7 appendix support reliable comparison; rendered-page inspection confirms the visual material is available.

before.justification: v3 reports original VIRES evaluations on VIRESET and DAVIS, human-preference studies, ablations, and appendix experiments on architecture variants, additional conditions, and sketch sparsity.

after.justification: v6 retains these original quantitative, qualitative, human-preference, and appendix results in Sections 5 and 7, including Tables 1 and 3–5.

M1.justification: The Sequential ControlNet, standardized self-scaling, sketch attention, sketch-aware encoder, losses, and inference procedures are unchanged. The sparse-guidance and long-video adaptations are also retained.

E1.justification: Both use VIRESET and DAVIS and retain the same editing applications, edge/depth conditioning evaluations, sparse-sketch scenarios, and long-duration demonstrations. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Rerender, VidToMe, Text2Video-Zero, RAVE, and VideoComposer. The appendix comparisons also retain their comparator membership, including VideoComposer for sketch-to-video generation and inpainting.

E3.justification: Both report the same training stages, 51-frame evaluation clips, 50 sampled videos per dataset, five quantitative metrics, and human-study design. Appendix training budgets and sketch-sparsity settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The four component ablations in Section 5.3 and the architecture, edge/depth-conditioning, and sketch-sparsity analyses in Sections 7.1–7.3 are identical. The same qualitative application demonstrations remain.

E5.justification: Point estimates and human-preference percentages retain the same reporting practices. Neither version reports experimental seed/run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1 and 3–5 and the qualitative result panels are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains VIRES PSNR values of 23.87 on VIRESET and 25.36 on DAVIS.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and their mathematical definitions, including flow matching, latent masking, feature modulation, attention, and training losses, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework and dataset contributions, application scope, novelty positioning, and claims of superior editing quality and human preference.

C2.justification: The component-effect interpretations, explanation of stronger self-scaling benefits for edges than depth, and potential backbone compatibility are retained. The computational limitation remains 323 seconds per 51-frame clip on an A6000, approximately 1.6 times slower than the cited alternatives.

D1.justification: The abstract's project address changes from suimuc.github.io/suimu.github.io/projects/VIRES/ to hjzheng.net/projects/VIRES/, revising access information. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether resource availability changed.

R1.justification: The same 53 references and research-positioning discussions remain. Changed citation-page backlinks for references 48 and 53 reflect text reflow, not changes in cited works or their interpretation.

P1.justification: The project-page line and arXiv version/date notice receive small textual updates. Scientific prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1's comparison and ablation group headings become larger and bold. The abstract and early paragraphs reflow, with small spacing adjustments. Figure panels, table structures, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 preserves the complete scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations, and implementation details, including the appendix analyses. The project-address update and small typography changes, chiefly Table 1's group headings, do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
